title: U.S. House · Florida's 19th District
area: Southwest Florida including Cape Coral, Fort Myers, and Estero, under Florida's 2026 congressional map.

context.text: Florida's U.S. House elections use a new congressional map for 2026; Gov. Ron DeSantis signed the new district boundaries into law on May 4, 2026.

Incumbent Rep. Byron Donalds (R) did not make the ballot for this district; the seat is open. Jim Schwartzel won a crowded Republican primary on August 18, 2026 that also included former Rep. Madison Cawthorn and former state Sen. Catalina Lauf, among others. Victor Arias won the Democratic primary, defeating Robert Neeld and Howard Sapp.
Alexandra Zakhvatayev is running as a write-in candidate with no party affiliation.

candidates.name: Victor Arias
candidates.currentRole: Attorney (Owner and Managing Attorney, Arias Law Firm)

summary.text: Victor Arias is an attorney and law firm owner in Cape Coral who won the Democratic primary for the open 19th District seat on August 18, 2026. According to Ballotpedia, he has worked as an attorney and business owner; he describes his campaign as centered on economic affordability, water quality, and anti-corruption.

background.text: Describes himself as one of eight children raised in the Douglas Housing Projects in New York.
Earned a high school diploma from Lawrence Academy and a bachelor's degree from Hamilton College in 1985, according to Ballotpedia.
Is a member of the Florida Bar and says he has practiced law for over 35 years; he is owner and managing attorney of Arias Law Firm, P.A. in Cape Coral.

Is a graduate of Leadership Florida, Leadership Lee County, Leadership Cape Coral, and Leadership Estero, and says he received the Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr. Service Award and the Hispanic Chamber Businessman of the Year Award.
Says he has mentored high school and college students by welcoming them to his law firm.
Won the August 18, 2026 Democratic primary with 45.5% of the vote, ahead of Howard Sapp and Robert Neeld. This is his first campaign for federal office listed by Ballotpedia.
Says he has been married for 32 years and has two children who attend universities.

priorities.text: Says he will work to diversify the economy and create jobs to address high costs for gas, groceries, utilities, and insurance.
Says he will defend Southwest Florida water quality through Everglades restoration, red tide research funding, and Lake Okeechobee discharge reforms.
Says he wants Congress to reclaim its constitutional lawmaking responsibility from the courts through stronger ethics and budget oversight.

positions.summary: As an immigration attorney, says he supports a humane approach and fair treatment for immigrants pursuing legal status while saying he does not condone breaking the law.
Supports Everglades restoration, red tide research funding, and Lake Okeechobee discharge reforms to protect water quality.

candidates.name: Jim Schwartzel
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 18, 2026 Republican primary in a crowded field

summary.text: Jim Schwartzel is a Southwest Florida broadcaster and publisher who won the Republican primary for the open 19th District seat on August 18, 2026. He owns and operates conservative radio stations and a local newspaper publisher. In his Candidate Connection survey he describes himself as a businessman and outsider and says he is running to support President Trump's agenda.

background.text: Was born in Naples, Florida, according to Ballotpedia, and describes himself as a lifelong Southwest Florida resident.
Graduated from Bishop Verot High School in Fort Myers and earned a bachelor's degree from Stetson University in 1998.
Says his first job, at age 12, was watering and sweeping the clay tennis courts at The Landings in Fort Myers.

Is president of Sun Broadcasting; according to The Floridian, he owns and operates 92.5 FOX News and Trump County 93.7 Radio in Southwest Florida and owns Gulfshore Life Media, which publishes the Naples Press.

Announced his candidacy in April 2025, after Rep. Byron Donalds said he would not seek re-election and would run for governor. He described himself to reporters as a non-politician and said he would buy his own ads on his stations rather than block other candidates' ads.
Won the August 18, 2026 Republican primary in a field of ten candidates with 29.1% of the vote.
According to his campaign survey, he is married to Carly and they have two children.

priorities.text: Says Washington needs business leaders rather than career politicians, and campaigns on cutting spending and opposing overregulation.
Supports securing the border, deporting people in the country illegally, and finishing construction of a border wall.
Supports tax cuts and policies aimed at increasing domestic energy production.

positions.summary: Supports Trump administration border security policies, including deportations and completing a border wall.
positions.quote: No nation can survive without borders—I will support Trump's policies to secure the border, deport illegal immigrants, and finish the wall.

positions.summary: Campaigns for tax cuts rather than tax increases.
positions.quote: I will fight for Trump-style tax cuts that reward hard work and keep businesses in America.

positions.summary: Says he will stand with law enforcement and opposes what he calls soft-on-crime policies.
positions.quote: Crime is skyrocketing because soft-on-crime liberals refuse to enforce the law—I will stand with law enforcement and back the blue.

summary.text: Seth Haskin is running with no party affiliation in the general election for Florida's 19th District. Ballotpedia lists a career as a business manager and a 2022 bachelor's degree. His campaign centers on increasing the size of the U.S. House and on constitutional and structural reform proposals.

background.text: Earned a high school diploma from St. Croix Falls High School and a bachelor's degree from Bethel University in 2022, according to Ballotpedia.
Says he comes from a lower middle-class background and has a bachelor's degree in neuroscience.
Lists his career experience as business manager, according to Ballotpedia.
Describes his main goal in Congress as increasing the size of the House of Representatives and says he supports a literal interpretation of the Constitution.

priorities.text: Says his biggest goal in Congress is to increase the size of the House of Representatives, which he says would connect representatives to constituents, make gerrymandering more difficult, and help root out corruption.
Says Congress, not unelected bureaucrats, should write the laws, and calls for restoring the non-delegation doctrine and ending what he calls government by regulation.
Says he would support restoring state legislative selection of U.S. senators, reversing the 17th Amendment's direct election of senators.

candidates.name: Alexandra Zakhvatayev

summary.text: Alexandra Zakhvatayev is a write-in candidate with no party affiliation for Florida's 19th District. Beyond her ballot listing, no biographical information or campaign materials were found.

candidates.researchNotes: Checked Alexandra Zakhvatayev's own Ballotpedia page (https://ballotpedia.org/Alexandra_Zakhvatayev): no biography, no completed 2026 Candidate Connection survey, no campaign website, and no news coverage found. Only personal Facebook and LinkedIn links are listed with no accessible content.

sources.title: Jim Schwartzel Announces Bid to Replace Byron Donalds in Congressional District 19

researchNotes: This is an open seat after incumbent Byron Donalds did not make the ballot. No biographical information found for write-in candidate Alexandra Zakhvatayev beyond her ballot listing; no campaign website found for Victor Arias, Jim Schwartzel (site blocked), or Seth Haskin, so biographies rely on Ballotpedia and, for Schwartzel, one news report.
